what: Green-start arms: installing the template into an empty project from the public repository
why_here: The raw evidence — six run logs with reasoning traces, one manual-arm log, and seven installed repositories — is deliberately NOT in this repository. Two reasons, in order. It carries employer-identifying strings (a work email domain in one log and in one working tree's .git/config, and a work account name in four logs), and docs/constraints.md binds this public repository against that, including in history; the pre-commit scan would not have caught it, because its patterns match credential values and not identifiers, by design. And the installed trees are ~400 KB each of near-unmodified skeleton, reconstructible from .template-version and install.sh. This file is the summary §8 anticipates for exactly that case: 'reproducible without the raw, possibly gitignored, data behind it'.
verify: sha256 of each raw file is recorded below. A later reader with the raw evidence can confirm it is the artefact these records cite; without it, the outcomes here stand on their own.

outcomes_measured.invented: Was anything stated about the project that the operator did not supply
outcomes_measured.note: Both were pre-registered in CHECKPOINT-install-path.md before runs 4-1, 4-2 and 5 were performed. For the three earlier arms they are applied retrospectively, which is weaker and is marked per row.

arms.note: Owner: filled with a git address, which the register's own preamble forbids. Two <<FILL: markers answered leaving their closing bracket, in the two session-loaded files, and check.sh reported ok.

arms.cost: 12 min 11 s to a verified install
arms.note: Endpoint was 'installed', not 'ready to work' — seven blanks unanswered, nothing committed. Project name taken from the folder rather than the brief, producing a wrong title nothing detected. A lower bound: the operator had seen the project before.

Three success criteria with named metrics, three stakeholder categories where one was given, four scope exclusions — none supplied. The trace records it as a decision: 'the user didn't provide specific prompts, so I can avoid creating new questions'. The Python/uv stack it named was NOT invention: the skeleton asserted it and AGENTS.md instructed a match.

Invention stopped. The register was still avoided: the trace weighs the withdrawn Owner: rule — 'asking could block progress' — and concludes that keeping OPEN_QUESTIONS.md as a shipped template is best. Deleted DATA_ENVIRONMENT.md and updated the INDEX artifact table to say why.
arms.record: EXP-2026-08-26-green-start-assisted (superseded reading); the withdrawal is in v3.3.0

arms.note: Run 1. Entries raised with Owner: blank, which the amended preamble sanctions. Measures cause A against exp_a-3, confounded by the CLI moving v1.0.80 to v1.0.81 between them.

Run 1-prime, the variance probe: identical condition to exp_a-4-1, thirteen minutes later. Both binary outcomes identical, so the stopping rule did not fire. The entry COUNT differed, 2 against 1, which is why the coarse outcomes were fixed in advance.

Run 2, the marker flags removed. Same CLI build as both prior runs, so no harness confound. Neither outcome moved. Left the shipped Q-<slug> placeholder standing beside three real entries; not attributed to the treatment. The 1-2-3 entry-count trend across the three runs is refused as unreadable in the record.

design_inputs.what: the design and the frozen prompt, identical across every arm
